intro: Had a UK visa refused? Our visa refusal help starts with reading your refusal letter carefully, explaining why it happened and what your options are, then preparing a stronger fresh application where that is the right route.

rules.title: Deadlines are strict
rules.text: Administrative review and appeal deadlines are short, often 14 days from inside the UK or 28 days from outside. Contact us straight away.

rules.title: Appeals and reviews
rules.text: Our advisers are regulated by the IAA at Level 1. We review your refusal and advise on your options, and where an appeal or administrative review is needed, we refer you to a representative authorised to handle it.

rules.title: Declare previous refusals
rules.text: Every future application must declare a refusal. A well-prepared fresh application can still succeed.

boxTitle: Want a second pair of eyes before you apply?
boxText: A consultation costs far less than a refused application. We’ll check your case against the current rules and tell you honestly where you stand.

sections.heading: How our visa refusal help works
sections.text: We read the refusal letter with you, explain each reason in plain English, and look at whether the problem was evidence, eligibility or how the application was presented. We then tell you honestly whether a fresh application is likely to succeed and what it would need.

faqs.q: Can I reapply after a visa refusal?
faqs.a: Usually yes, once you’ve fixed the reasons for the refusal. You must declare the refusal.

faqs.q: Is there a deadline after a refusal?
faqs.a: If you have a right to administrative review or appeal, there are strict deadlines. Check your letter and contact us straight away.
We advise on your options and refer appeal work to an authorised representative where needed.
